user.title: Main fuse
user.description: The guard keeps every phase below the fuse rating minus the safety margin.

data_description.margin_a: The guard starts cutting at fuse minus margin, e.g. 15.4 A for a 16 A fuse with 0.6 A margin.
data_description.voltage: Used to convert amps to watts.

meters.title: Meters on your main fuse
meters.description: Found {count} meters with a current sensor per phase. Pick every one that measures the current through your main fuse (not a single circuit, an EV charger or a solar inverter's own output). The next step fills in their sensors, and you can still change them there. Pick none to choose sensors yourself.

sources.title: Phase current sensors
sources.description: Pick every sensor that measures each phase. The guard uses the highest fresh reading, so extra meters only make it safer. Meters that label phases A/B/C are filled in as A = L1, B = L2, C = L3; the next step checks whether that is right.

data_description.freshness_s: A reading older than this is ignored. If no reading on a phase is fresh, the guard fails safe.

check.title: Check the phase sensors

load.title: Controllable load
load.description: Pick the setpoint the guard may turn down, what the load wants when there is room, and when the guard is allowed to write.

data_description.setpoint_entity: The number entity in W that the guard turns down, for example a battery's forced-charge power.
data_description.target_entity: What the load wants when there is room, for example the charge power your scheduler asks for. Use this or a fixed target, not both.
data_description.target_w: Used when no target entity is set.
data_description.active_conditions: Optional. The guard only changes the setpoint while all these conditions hold, for example while the battery is in forced-charge mode. Leave empty if the load is always active.
data_description.load_phases: The phases the load draws from. The guard uses this to work out how many watts each amp of overload costs.

feedback.name: Feedback from the device (optional)
feedback.description: Lets the guard check that the device follows its commands. Without these it trusts the setpoint.

data_description.readback_entity: The value the device actually holds, often a sensor with the same name as the setpoint. Defaults to the setpoint's own state.
data_description.actual_entity: The power the load really draws. With it, the guard won't give more power to a load that isn't following.
data_description.actual_sign: Whether this sensor is positive or negative while the load draws power. The next step warns if it looks wrong.

error.margin_too_large: The margin must be smaller than the fuse.
error.no_sensors: Pick at least one sensor for this phase.
error.not_amps: All sensors must report in A.
error.target_one_of: Set either a target entity or a fixed target, not both.
error.not_watts: The setpoint must be in W.
error.above_setpoint_max: The target is above the setpoint's maximum.

advanced.title: Advanced timing
advanced.description: Defaults are tuned for a battery that follows a new setpoint in about 10 s.

data_description.min_over_a: How far over the threshold counts as a real overload.
data_description.base_drop_w: Each cut is this plus the overload converted to watts.
data_description.response_s: A further cut needs a phase reading taken at least this long after the previous cut.
data_description.recovery_gain: Share of the measured headroom given back per recovery step, and allowed when the load turns on.
data_description.on_missing_data: Only applies while the load is active.
